questions.question: Which mathematical property of the Fourier Transform explains why time-domain convolution corresponds to frequency-domain multiplication?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Linearity refers to the superposition property of the transform.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Duality relates time and frequency domain roles but not convolution directly.
explanations.c: Correct! The Convolution Theorem states that convolution in time is multiplication in frequency.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Time-shifting affects the phase of the Fourier Transform.

questions.question: What effect does time reversal have on the Fourier Transform of a signal x(t)?

answers.a: It results in a phase shift.
answers.b: It produces the complex conjugate of the Fourier Transform.
answers.c: It reflects the Fourier Transform about the origin.
answers.d: It shifts the Fourier Transform by a constant frequency.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Time reversal doesn't introduce a phase shift.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Complex conjugation occurs under different transformations.
explanations.c: Correct! Time reversal reflects the Fourier Transform about the origin.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Time reversal does not shift the spectrum.

questions.question: If x(t) is real and even, what is the nature of its Fourier Transform X(f)?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Real and even signals produce real and even transforms.
explanations.b: Correct! The Fourier Transform of a real and even function is also real and even.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Oddness does not result from even time signals.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The transform is even, not odd.

questions.question: Why does a rectangular window in the time domain lead to spectral leakage in the frequency domain?

answers.a: Because the Fourier Transform of a rectangular function is a Gaussian.
answers.b: Because the time-domain window is not smooth, causing sinc-like ripples in frequency.
answers.c: Because the rectangular window causes frequency-domain aliasing.
answers.d: Because it increases the resolution in the frequency domain.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The Fourier Transform of a rectangle is a sinc, not Gaussian.
explanations.b: Correct! Abrupt truncation in time causes spreading in frequency, resulting in spectral leakage.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Aliasing is a sampling issue, not a windowing effect.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Rectangular windows decrease frequency resolution due to leakage.

questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary condition for a signal to have a Fourier Transform?

answers.c: The signal must be absolutely integrable.
answers.d: The signal must have finite bandwidth.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Non-periodic signals can also have Fourier Transforms.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Complex-valued signals can also have Fourier Transforms.
explanations.c: Correct! A necessary condition is that the signal be absolutely integrable.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Finite bandwidth is not a requirement for existence.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the bandwidth of a signal and the width of its Fourier Transform?

answers.a: The bandwidth is inversely proportional to the width of the Fourier Transform.
answers.b: The bandwidth is directly proportional to the width of the Fourier Transform.
answers.c: The bandwidth is unaffected by the Fourier Transform.
answers.d: The bandwidth is related to the phase spectrum of the Fourier Transform.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The relationship is direct, not inverse.
explanations.b: Correct! The bandwidth of a signal is directly proportional to the width of its Fourier Transform.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The Fourier Transform affects the bandwidth of the signal.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The bandwidth is related to the magnitude spectrum, not the phase.

questions.question: What is the Fourier Transform of a triangular pulse?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The Fourier Transform of a rectangular pulse results in a sinc function.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Gaussian functions are not related to triangular pulses.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The Fourier Transform of a triangular pulse is not another triangular pulse.
explanations.d: Correct! The Fourier Transform of a triangular pulse is a sinc function squared.

questions.question: If a signal x(t) is scaled in time as x(at), what happens to its Fourier Transform X(f)?

answers.a: The Fourier Transform is scaled by the same factor a in frequency.
answers.b: The Fourier Transform is scaled by the reciprocal factor 1/|a| along frequency, with amplitude also scaled by 1/|a|.
answers.c: The Fourier Transform is shifted in frequency by a constant a.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Time scaling does not directly scale frequencies by a; it is reciprocal.
explanations.b: Correct! x(at) results in X(f/a)/|a| in the Fourier domain — the spectrum is inversely scaled and the amplitude adjusted by 1/|a|.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Scaling does not shift the spectrum; shifting is a different operation.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Scaling in time always affects the Fourier Transform.

questions.question: What is the Fourier Transform of a signal x(t) sampled at a rate fs?

answers.a: The Fourier Transform is periodic with period fs.
answers.b: The Fourier Transform is continuous with no periodicity.
answers.c: The Fourier Transform has a frequency shift by fs.
answers.d: The Fourier Transform is a sinc function.

explanations.a: Correct! The Fourier Transform of a sampled signal is periodic with a period equal to the sampling rate fs.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The Fourier Transform of a sampled signal is periodic.
explanations.c: Incorrect. There is no frequency shift by fs.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The Fourier Transform is not necessarily a sinc function.

questions.question: What happens to the Fourier Transform of a signal when the signal is convolved with a filter in the time domain?

answers.a: The Fourier Transform of the signal is multiplied by the Fourier Transform of the filter.
answers.b: The Fourier Transform of the signal is shifted in frequency.
answers.c: The Fourier Transform is unaffected by convolution.
answers.d: The Fourier Transform of the signal is convolved with the Fourier Transform of the filter.

explanations.a: Correct! Convolution in the time domain corresponds to multiplication in the frequency domain.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Convolution in the time domain does not cause a frequency shift.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Convolution in the time domain does affect the Fourier Transform.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Multiplication in the frequency domain corresponds to convolution in the time domain.
